title: the page asks back
subtitle: one real question, "hey", riding the loop end to end

pipeline.title: the pipeline, one real question, today's run

steps.text: you select text and press Ask, the page POSTs one json record
questions.jsonl gains one line, next to the html
the waiter sees 1 question and 0 answers, exits: the wake signal
the session that built the page answers, answers.jsonl gains a line
the page polls, the card fills, the selection turns yellow

pipeline.foot: this record is real, it rode the loop earlier today

stops.headline: The blue survives the click because the range is cloned before focus moves

lines: you select text, the browser paints it blue
the range is cloned the instant Ask is pressed

result.text: the blue holds while you type,
result.note: and turns yellow when you send

lines: you select text, the browser paints it blue

result.note: you type blind, not knowing what you asked about

think.claim: a chip only appears for a real selection
proofs: two characters minimum, inside the page, never inside the ask box itself

think.claim: a question always knows where it came from
proofs: the enclosing stop id travels with the record
so the card finds its home again after any reload

stops.headline: A 64 KB cap and a lock stand between the page and the questions file

think.claim: two clicks can land in the same instant
proofs: the append holds a lock, the server is threaded

think.claim: a question outlives both the server and the session
proofs: it is a line in a file, so whoever runs the waiter next can answer it

stops.headline: The waiter exiting is the wake signal, the model never polls

hops.label: files_signature()
hops.desc: the loop only re-parses when a file actually moved

hops.label: pending = questions - answers
hops.desc: pending is question ids minus answer ids, so a crash re-surfaces the same question

hops.label: print + exit 0
hops.desc: the process dying is the signal; nothing polls a model

hops.label: --answer <id>
hops.desc: answer text arrives on stdin, so shell quoting never touches it

think.claim: the answering session is the session that built the page
proofs: so it answers with the diff, the conversation, and your skills in hand
which is why a question about fake test data still got the real answer

stops.headline: A card finds its home and its yellow mark from the record alone

block.mermaid:
flowchart TD
    A[you select text and press Ask] --> B[POST /ask]
    B -->|64 KB cap, one lock| C[(questions.jsonl)]
    C --> D{waiter: any id without an answer}
    D -->|exit 0, the wake signal| E[the building session answers]
    E --> F[(answers.jsonl)]
    F -->|poll every 2s| G([card fills, mark turns yellow])
    G --> A
block.caption: every node is a code reference, the loop closes because an answered card can be quoted again

think.claim: a mark is re-found from its text, never from pixels
proofs: the stored selection is searched inside its own stop first
if the text changed, that one mark drops and the card says so

discussion.quote: the answering session is the session that built the page
discussion.question: what if that session is gone?
discussion.answer:
- the question stays in the file, nothing is lost
- a fresh session can answer it, it just re-reads the code instead of remembering the build

replies.question: so the answers get worse?
replies.answer:
- narrower, not wrong
- it loses why a choice was made, and keeps what the code says
